requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/bilateral-receipt-other-request

specRefs.section: §6 Public-key resolution (dual-shape) and §8 Composition with bilateral receipts

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the bilateral-receipt request with a receipt the responder signed for another request: receiptPayloadJcs.initiatorSignatureBase64 is the Envoys §14 Vector 1 signature, not the signature of this request. The responder signature verifies, but the receipt does not acknowledge this request. A conforming A2A-IDF verifier MUST reject it (RECEIPT_MISMATCH).

requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/bilateral-receipt-signature-tampered

specRefs.section: §6 Public-key resolution (dual-shape) and §8 Composition with bilateral receipts

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the bilateral-receipt request and receipt with the responder signature altered (first base64 character changed). The receipt payload is unchanged, but the signature no longer verifies over its JCS form. A conforming A2A-IDF verifier MUST reject it (RECEIPT_SIGNATURE_INVALID).

requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/bilateral-receipt-status-mismatch

specRefs.section: §6 Public-key resolution (dual-shape) and §8 Composition with bilateral receipts

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the bilateral-receipt request with a receipt whose signed payload has status REJECTED while envelope.response.status reads ACCEPTED. The responder signature verifies, but the response states a status the responder did not sign. A conforming A2A-IDF verifier MUST reject it (RECEIPT_MISMATCH).

requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/bilateral-receipt

specRefs.section: §6 Public-key resolution (dual-shape) and §8 Composition with bilateral receipts

requirements.description: A2A-IDF identity-framework wrap of an Envoys §14 Vector 2 wire signature (POST /api/task with a JSON body) inside an APS bilateral-receipt envelope. The initiator's wire signature is byte-identical to Envoys §14 Vector 2 by construction (the envelope does not re-sign the wire request). The envelope adds a responder acknowledgment: the responder's Ed25519 signature over the JCS-canonical receipt payload, which names the initiator's wire signature. Both reference verifiers check the wire layer (RFC 9421 + A2A-IDF §6 dual-shape keyid resolution) and then the envelope: the responder signature over the receipt payload, and that the payload acknowledges this request's signature and initiator and matches the response members beside it.

requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/body-tampered

specRefs.section: §6 Public-key resolution (dual-shape: application/did+json vs compact form)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the bilateral-receipt request body modified after signing (url changed to https://evil.example/doc), with the Content-Digest header recomputed to match the new body — as an in-path attacker who cannot re-sign would do. The Signature header still carries the Envoys §14 Vector 2 signature over the ORIGINAL body's signature base. A conforming A2A-IDF verifier MUST reject: content-digest is a signed component, so the recomputed digest changes the signature base and Ed25519 verification fails.

requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/cross-suite-mismatch

specRefs.section: §6 Public-key resolution (dual-shape: application/did+json vs compact form)
§7.1 Test 2 (signing key and resolved public key)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the signature-alone request signed by a different valid Ed25519 key (RFC 8032 §7.1 Test 2), with the DID Document serving that same key, so the Signature header verifies against the resolved key. The fixture still declares byte-identity with Envoys §14 Vector 1, and its expected.signatureBase64 field carries the Vector 1 bytes instead of the bytes in the Signature header. A conforming verifier MUST reject: the cross-suite byte-match is a claim about the signature the verifier checked, so it compares the bytes parsed from the Signature header with the pinned vector, and those are the Test 2 signature. A verifier that compares expected.signatureBase64 instead accepts this fixture.

requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/delegation-chain-3link

specRefs.section: §14 Vector 3 (POST request, empty JSON object body)

requirements.description: A2A-IDF identity-framework wrap of an Envoys §14 Vector 3 wire signature (POST /api/echo with an empty JSON object body) inside a 3-link APS delegation chain envelope. The wire signature is byte-identical to Envoys §14 Vector 3 by construction. The envelope adds three signed delegation links demonstrating the chain rules from A2A-IDF §7: scope monotonic narrowing, expiry monotonic non-increase, depth at most maxDepth, and previousSignature binding between consecutive links. Both reference verifiers check the wire layer (RFC 9421 + A2A-IDF §6 dual-shape keyid resolution) and then the chain: its depth, each link's issuer and its Ed25519 signature over the JCS form of the link payload, scope narrowing and expiry non-increase from link to link, and that the last link delegates to the wire keyid with a scope that grants the request.

requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/delegation-chain-depth-exceeded

specRefs.section: §14 Vector 3 (POST request, empty JSON object body)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the delegation-chain-3link request and chain with envelope.maxDepth set to 2. Every link is signed by its issuer and the chain rules hold, but the chain has 3 links, more than maxDepth allows. A conforming A2A-IDF verifier MUST reject it (DEPTH_EXCEEDED).

requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/delegation-chain-expiry-extended

specRefs.section: §14 Vector 3 (POST request, empty JSON object body)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the delegation-chain-3link chain with the expiresAt of the last link set to 2099-01-01T00:00:00Z, signed by its issuer. Every link verifies, but the last link expires after the link before it (2026-09-30T00:00:00Z). A conforming A2A-IDF verifier MUST reject it (EXPIRY_EXTENDED).

requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/delegation-chain-issuer-not-delegate

specRefs.section: §14 Vector 3 (POST request, empty JSON object body)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the delegation-chain-3link chain with its last link issued by did:web:counterparty.example:agents:delegate-level-3, which envelope.keyidResolutions resolves, instead of delegate-level-2, the subject of the link before it. The link is signed by its issuer's key, so its signature verifies, but nothing in the chain delegates to delegate-level-3. A conforming A2A-IDF verifier MUST reject it (CHAIN_BROKEN).

requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/delegation-chain-leaf-not-signer

specRefs.section: §14 Vector 3 (POST request, empty JSON object body)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the delegation-chain-3link chain with its last link delegating to did:web:counterparty.example:agents:delegate-level-3 instead of the wire keyid, signed by its issuer. Every link verifies and the chain rules hold, but the chain does not end at the key that signed the request. A conforming A2A-IDF verifier MUST reject it (CHAIN_BROKEN).

requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/delegation-chain-link-replaced

specRefs.section: §14 Vector 3 (POST request, empty JSON object body)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the delegation-chain-3link chain with link 1 replaced by another link from the same issuer to the same subject, with scope [POST /api/echo], which that issuer signed over the root's signature. The replacement verifies, but link 2 was signed over the signature of the link 1 it was issued under (its previousSignature), so link 2 no longer verifies. A conforming A2A-IDF verifier MUST reject it (LINK_SIGNATURE_INVALID).

requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/delegation-chain-link-tampered

specRefs.section: §14 Vector 3 (POST request, empty JSON object body)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the delegation-chain-3link chain with the expiresAt of link 1 moved from 2026-09-30T00:00:00Z to 2026-08-31T00:00:00Z after the link was signed. Expiry still does not increase along the chain, but the signature of link 1 no longer verifies over its payload. A conforming A2A-IDF verifier MUST reject it (LINK_SIGNATURE_INVALID).

requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/delegation-chain-request-out-of-scope

specRefs.section: §14 Vector 3 (POST request, empty JSON object body)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the delegation-chain-3link chain with the scope of the last link narrowed to [POST /api/health], signed by its issuer. Every link verifies and every scope narrows the one before it, but the last link does not grant the request, POST /api/echo. A conforming A2A-IDF verifier MUST reject it (REQUEST_OUT_OF_SCOPE).

requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/delegation-chain-root-tampered

specRefs.section: §14 Vector 3 (POST request, empty JSON object body)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the delegation-chain-3link chain with DELETE /api/everything added to the scope of the root link after the root was signed. The links after it are unchanged and still narrow that scope, but the root signature no longer verifies over the root payload. A conforming A2A-IDF verifier MUST reject it (LINK_SIGNATURE_INVALID).

requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/delegation-chain-scope-widened

specRefs.section: §14 Vector 3 (POST request, empty JSON object body)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the delegation-chain-3link chain with DELETE /api/everything added to the scope of the last link, signed by its issuer. Every link verifies and the last link still grants the request, but it grants an entry that the link before it does not hold. A conforming A2A-IDF verifier MUST reject it (SCOPE_WIDENED).

requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/key-substituted

specRefs.section: §6 Public-key resolution (dual-shape: application/did+json vs compact form)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the signature-alone request with the DID Document's verification keys substituted for a different valid Ed25519 key (RFC 8032 §7.1 Test 2, in both publicKeyMultibase and publicKeyJwk encodings). The signature bytes are the valid Envoys §14 Vector 1 signature, produced by the Test 1 key. A conforming A2A-IDF verifier MUST reject: the key material served at the keyid URL does not match the signing key. Models a key-substitution attack on the §6 resolution step — the resolved document is attacker-controlled but cannot validate a signature it did not produce.

requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/signature-alone

specRefs.section: §6 Public-key resolution (dual-shape: application/did+json vs compact form)

requirements.description: A2A-IDF identity-framework wrap of an Envoys §14 Vector 1 wire signature. The keyid URL resolves to a W3C DID Document (Ed25519VerificationKey2020 + publicKeyMultibase) rather than the Envoys §6 compact form. Because the RFC 9421 signature base depends only on the signed components and parameters, not on the keyid document shape, the resulting signature is byte-identical to Envoys §14 Vector 1. This fixture demonstrates that a verifier implementing A2A-IDF §6 dual-shape keyid resolution can interoperate with Envoys-signed traffic without re-keying or re-signing.

requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/signature-tag-absent

specRefs.section: §6 Public-key resolution (dual-shape: application/did+json vs compact form)

requirements.description: The absent half of the §4.3 tag pair: the signature-alone request (Envoys §14 Vector 1) with no tag parameter. An absent tag is treated as `a2a-message` for back-compat, so a conforming verifier MUST accept it. Paired with signature-tag-foreign, which differs only in carrying a tag other than `a2a-message`: a verifier that requires an explicit tag fails this fixture, and one that ignores the tag fails the other.

requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/signature-tag-foreign-tampered

specRefs.section: §6 Public-key resolution (dual-shape: application/did+json vs compact form)

requirements.description: Check-order fixture with two defects: the signature-alone request carries tag="not-a2a-message" (a TAG_MISMATCH) and its Ed25519 signature bytes are altered in the first base64 character (a SIGNATURE_INVALID). The §4.3 tag rule is an application requirement on the signature parameters and is applied before key resolution and signature verification, so a conforming verifier MUST reject with TAG_MISMATCH. A verifier that checks the signature first reports SIGNATURE_INVALID and fails this fixture. signature-tag-foreign cannot pin this order: its signature verifies, so both orders reject it with TAG_MISMATCH.

requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/signature-tag-foreign

specRefs.section: §6 Public-key resolution (dual-shape: application/did+json vs compact form)

requirements.description: Negative fixture, the foreign half of the §4.3 tag pair: the signature-alone request signed with tag="not-a2a-message" by the correct key. Content-Digest, signature base, Signature-Input, keyid resolution and the Ed25519 signature are all valid. A conforming verifier MUST reject: the tag says the signature was produced for an application other than A2A messaging, and only `a2a-message` or an absent tag is accepted. Models cross-application replay of a signature that verifies. The tag check runs before the Ed25519 check, so the reject category is TAG_MISMATCH.

requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/signature-tag-null

specRefs.section: §6 Public-key resolution (dual-shape: application/did+json vs compact form)

requirements.description: The signature-alone request (Envoys §14 Vector 1) with signatureParams.tag set to JSON null. A null tag is an absent tag: it is omitted from the @signature-params line and from the Signature-Input header, never serialized as tag="null". The signature base, and therefore the signature, are byte-identical to Vector 1. Pins identical null handling across verifiers: a verifier that serializes the null reconstructs a different base and fails at the signature-base stage.

requirements.name: aim-did-rfc9421/signature-tampered

specRefs.section: §6 Public-key resolution (dual-shape: application/did+json vs compact form)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the signature-alone request with its Ed25519 signature bytes tampered (first base64 character altered). Everything else — body, Content-Digest, signature base, Signature-Input, keyid resolution — is identical to the valid fixture. A conforming A2A-IDF verifier MUST reject the request: the signature no longer verifies against the resolved public key. Models in-flight modification of the Signature header.

requirements.name: hippo-rfc9421/signature-alone-no-tag
requirements.description: Agent card GET without §4.3 tag (backward compat, absent ≡ a2a-message). Generated by lawcontinue/hippo-auth.

requirements.name: hippo-rfc9421/signature-alone-tag
requirements.description: A2A message POST with §4.3 tag=a2a-message. Generated by lawcontinue/hippo-auth, conformant signature base per RFC 9421 §2.3.

requirements.name: levels/level-0-agent-id-malformed

specRefs.section: §1 Agent Identity Verification Levels — Agent Identifiers (URN format)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: a SELF_ASSERTED AgentCard whose agentId is not in the urn:a2a:agent:{domain}:{agent-name}:{version} format required by A2A-IDF §1 for declared agent identifiers. A conforming verifier MUST reject the declaration shape: a malformed agentId cannot serve as a stable identifier across AgentCard updates and key rotations.

requirements.name: levels/level-0-agent-id-null

specRefs.section: §1 Agent Identity Verification Levels — Agent Identifiers (declared agentId with a null value)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: a SELF_ASSERTED AgentCard whose agentId member is JSON null. A Level 0 card may omit agentId, but a member that is present declares an identifier, and null is not a urn:a2a:agent:{domain}:{agent-name}:{version} URN. A conforming verifier MUST reject the declaration shape. A verifier that reads a null member as an absent one accepts the card and fails this fixture.

requirements.name: levels/level-0-self-asserted

specRefs.section: §1 Agent Identity Verification Levels — Level 0 SELF_ASSERTED declaration shape

requirements.description: Level 0 (SELF_ASSERTED): an AgentCard declaring the agent-identity extension with identityLevel SELF_ASSERTED, a URN-format agentId, and an Ed25519 public key. No attestations are present and none are required — Level 0 makes no verifiable claim beyond well-formedness. A conforming verifier ACCEPTs the declaration shape while treating the identity as unverified (A2A-IDF Security Considerations: clients MUST NOT treat Level 0 agents as verified).

requirements.name: levels/level-1-agent-mismatch

specRefs.section: §1 Agent Identity Verification Levels — Level 1 DNS Verification (agent name binding)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the DOMAIN_VERIFIED AgentCard with a DNS TXT record whose agent field names a different agent under the same domain (agent=payments-bot, while the agentId names financial-advisor). Record name, kid, and fingerprint all match. A conforming verifier MUST reject: the domain owner endorsed this key for a different agent name. Models one agent reusing a record the domain published for another of its agents.

requirements.name: levels/level-1-attestations-not-array

specRefs.section: §1 Agent Identity Verification Levels — Level 1 DNS Verification (attestations array shape)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the DOMAIN_VERIFIED AgentCard whose attestations member is the domain attestation object itself, not an array holding it. Every other field, and the pinned DNS TXT record, is valid. A conforming verifier MUST reject at the shape stage: a value that is not an array carries no attestation, so the card has no domain attestation. A verifier that searches the value without checking its type raises instead of reaching a verdict and fails this fixture.

requirements.name: levels/level-1-domain-mismatch

specRefs.section: §1 Agent Identity Verification Levels — Level 1 DNS Verification (agentId domain binding)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the DOMAIN_VERIFIED AgentCard served from provider.url https://example.com, with a matching domain attestation and a valid DNS TXT record at _a2a-identity.example.com, but an agentId that claims a different domain (urn:a2a:agent:example.org:financial-advisor:v2). The agentId is a well-formed URN and the record's agent name, kid, and fingerprint all match. A conforming verifier MUST reject: the domain that endorsed the key is not the domain the agent identifier claims. Models an agent asserting an identifier under a domain it does not control while presenting another domain's record.

requirements.name: levels/level-1-domain-verified

specRefs.section: §1 Agent Identity Verification Levels — Level 1 DNS Verification (_a2a-identity TXT record)

requirements.description: Level 1 (DOMAIN_VERIFIED): an AgentCard declaring DOMAIN_VERIFIED with a domain attestation, plus the pinned DNS TXT record the domain owner published at _a2a-identity.example.com. A conforming verifier extracts the domain from provider.url, checks the record name, and verifies that the record's agent name matches the agentId, its kid matches the declared key ID, and its fp equals base64url(sha256(raw public key bytes)) without padding. All checks are offline against the pinned record — live DNS resolution (and DNSSEC) is deployment behavior outside the suite's scope.

requirements.name: levels/level-1-fingerprint-mismatch

specRefs.section: §1 Agent Identity Verification Levels — Level 1 DNS Verification (fingerprint binding)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the DOMAIN_VERIFIED AgentCard with a DNS TXT record whose fp field is the fingerprint of a DIFFERENT Ed25519 key (RFC 8032 §7.1 Test 2). Record name, agent name, and kid all match. A conforming verifier MUST reject: the fingerprint binds the DNS record to the exact public key bytes, and a mismatch means the domain owner did not endorse this key. Models an agent presenting a key the domain never authorized.

requirements.name: levels/level-1-idn-provider-url

specRefs.section: §1 Agent Identity Verification Levels — Level 1 DNS Verification (internationalized domain)

requirements.description: Level 1 (DOMAIN_VERIFIED) for an internationalized domain: provider.url is https://bücher.example, and every binding (attestation domain, agentId domain, DNS record name) uses its ASCII A-label xn--bcher-kva.example, the only form the agentId URN grammar and DNS admit. A conforming verifier derives the domain from provider.url in A-label form, as the WHATWG URL parser reports it, and ACCEPTs. A verifier that compares the Unicode host against the A-label bindings reports a spurious DOMAIN_MISMATCH.

requirements.name: levels/level-1-kid-mismatch

specRefs.section: §1 Agent Identity Verification Levels — Level 1 DNS Verification (kid binding)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the DOMAIN_VERIFIED AgentCard with a DNS TXT record whose kid field (agent-e5f6a7b8) differs from the declared publicKey.kid (agent-a1b2c3d4). Record name, agent name, and fingerprint all match. A conforming verifier MUST reject on the key ID binding before computing the fingerprint: the record endorses a key under a different identifier than the one the AgentCard declares. Models a card whose declared key ID drifted from the published record, for example after a key rotation that was not reflected in DNS.

requirements.name: levels/level-1-multi-defect-domain-and-version

specRefs.section: §1 Agent Identity Verification Levels — Level 1 DNS Verification (check order: record name before record version)

requirements.description: Check-order fixture with two defects: the DNS TXT record was published at _a2a-identity.example.net while provider.url is https://example.com (a DOMAIN_MISMATCH), and the record carries an unsupported version v=a2a9 (a SHAPE_INVALID). The record-name binding check precedes the record-version shape check in the contract order, so a conforming verifier MUST reject with DOMAIN_MISMATCH. A verifier that runs every shape check before any binding check reports SHAPE_INVALID and fails this fixture.

requirements.name: levels/level-1-provider-url-backslash-authority

specRefs.section: §1 Agent Identity Verification Levels — Level 1 DNS Verification (backslash in the provider.url authority)
URL parsing (authority state: a backslash ends the authority of a special scheme)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the DOMAIN_VERIFIED AgentCard whose provider.url is https://evil.example\@example.com (one backslash before the @). In an http or https URL a backslash ends the authority exactly as a slash does, so the host is evil.example and the rest is the path. The domain attestation, the agentId and the DNS TXT record all name example.com. A conforming verifier MUST reject: the provider domain is evil.example, which no binding names. A verifier whose URL parser reads the text before the @ as credentials derives example.com and accepts a card served from another host.

requirements.name: levels/level-1-provider-url-ignored-code-point

specRefs.section: §1 Agent Identity Verification Levels — Level 1 DNS Verification (ignored code point in the provider host)
domain to ASCII (UTS #46 ignored code points)

requirements.description: Level 1 (DOMAIN_VERIFIED) with a soft hyphen (U+00AD) in the provider host: provider.url is https://example.com with that code point between exam and ple, written as a JSON Unicode escape in this file. UTS #46 maps the soft hyphen to nothing, so the provider domain is example.com, which every binding names. A conforming verifier drops the ignored code point when it converts the domain to ASCII, as the WHATWG URL parser does, and ACCEPTs. A verifier that Punycode-encodes the label with the soft hyphen in it derives xn--example-oka.com and reports a spurious DOMAIN_MISMATCH.

requirements.name: levels/level-1-provider-url-ipv4-number

specRefs.section: §1 Agent Identity Verification Levels — Level 1 DNS Verification (numeric provider host)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the DOMAIN_VERIFIED AgentCard whose provider.url is https://0x7f.0.0.1, while the domain attestation, the agentId and the DNS TXT record name all spell the host the same way, 0x7f.0.0.1. A host whose last label is a number is an IPv4 address, and the WHATWG URL parser reports it in dotted-decimal form: the provider domain is 127.0.0.1. A conforming verifier MUST reject: no binding names 127.0.0.1. A verifier that compares the host as written accepts, and so treats two spellings of one address as two domains.

requirements.name: levels/level-1-provider-url-no-host

specRefs.section: §1 Agent Identity Verification Levels — Level 1 DNS Verification (provider.url without a host)
URL representation (a URL with an opaque path has a null host)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the DOMAIN_VERIFIED AgentCard whose provider.url is mailto:ops@example.com, a URL that has no host. The domain attestation, the agentId and the DNS TXT record all name example.com. A conforming verifier MUST reject at the shape stage: provider.url yields no provider domain to bind to. A verifier that takes the empty host as the domain reports DOMAIN_MISMATCH and fails this fixture.

requirements.name: levels/level-1-provider-url-not-string

specRefs.section: §1 Agent Identity Verification Levels — Level 1 DNS Verification (provider.url that is not a string)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the DOMAIN_VERIFIED AgentCard whose provider.url is an array holding the URL string https://example.com, not the string itself. The domain attestation, the agentId and the DNS TXT record all name example.com. A conforming verifier MUST reject at the shape stage: provider.url must be a string. A verifier that hands the value to a URL parser without checking its type can have it coerced to the string inside, derive example.com, and accept.

requirements.name: levels/level-1-provider-url-percent-encoded

specRefs.section: §1 Agent Identity Verification Levels — Level 1 DNS Verification (percent-encoded provider host)

requirements.description: Level 1 (DOMAIN_VERIFIED) with a percent-encoded provider host: provider.url is https://ex%61mple.com, where %61 is the letter a. Every binding names example.com. A conforming verifier percent-decodes the host before using it as the provider domain, as the WHATWG URL parser does, and ACCEPTs. A verifier that keeps the host as written, or refuses the percent sign, rejects and fails this fixture.

requirements.name: levels/level-1-provider-url-space-in-host

specRefs.section: §1 Agent Identity Verification Levels — Level 1 DNS Verification (provider.url with a forbidden host code point)

requirements.description: Negative fixture: the DOMAIN_VERIFIED AgentCard whose provider.url is https://exa mple.com, with a space inside the host. A space is a forbidden host code point, so the URL does not parse. The domain attestation, the agentId and the DNS TXT record all name example.com. A conforming verifier MUST reject at the shape stage: provider.url yields no provider domain. A verifier whose URL parser returns the host with the space in it reports DOMAIN_MISMATCH and fails this fixture.

requirements.name: levels/level-2-attestation-expired
requirements.description: Negative fixture: an ORGANIZATION_VERIFIED attestation whose registry signature is VALID but whose validity window ended before the pinned validationTime (expiresAt 2025-02-17 < validationTime 2026-07-03). Every other field is well-formed and correctly bound. A conforming verifier MUST reject on the validity window alone. The fixture pins validationTime so the expiry decision is deterministic and never depends on the wall clock.

requirements.name: levels/level-2-attestation-non-bmp-keys

specRefs.section: §3.2.3 Sorting of Object Properties (UTF-16 code units)

requirements.description: Level 2 (ORGANIZATION_VERIFIED): the valid organization attestation with one additional member, rfc8785SortingExample, whose property names are the RFC 8785 §3.2.3 sorting example. That set contains a key outside the Basic Multilingual Plane (U+1F600) and a key in U+E000-U+FFFF (U+FB33), so ordering by UTF-16 code units (required) and by Unicode code points (not conforming) produce different signing inputs. The registry signed the UTF-16-ordered JCS form. A conforming verifier includes the unknown member in the signing input, sorts it per RFC 8785 §3.2.3, and ACCEPTs; a verifier that sorts by code point reconstructs different bytes and rejects with SIGNATURE_INVALID.

requirements.name: levels/level-2-attestation-not-yet-valid
requirements.description: Negative fixture: an ORGANIZATION_VERIFIED attestation whose registry signature is VALID but whose validity window starts after the pinned validationTime (verifiedAt 2026-09-01 > validationTime 2026-07-03). Every other field is well-formed and correctly bound. A conforming verifier MUST reject on the validity window alone. Models an attestation presented before its issuer-stated start time; the fixture pins validationTime so the decision never depends on the wall clock.

requirements.name: levels/level-2-attestation-tampered
requirements.description: Negative fixture: the ORGANIZATION_VERIFIED attestation with subject.organization altered AFTER signing (Example Corp → Wrong Corp). The signature was produced over the original JCS form, so it no longer verifies against the modified content. A conforming verifier MUST reject. Models post-issuance modification of a registry attestation.

requirements.name: levels/level-2-issuer-not-object
requirements.description: Negative fixture: an ORGANIZATION_VERIFIED attestation whose issuer is a bare string (the registry name) instead of the {name, kid, url} object. Every other field is well-formed. A conforming verifier MUST reject at the shape stage, before any binding or signature check: a malformed field resolves to SHAPE_INVALID, never to an exception.

requirements.name: levels/level-2-jcs-utf16-key-order

specRefs.section: §3.2.3 Sorting of Object Properties (UTF-16 code units)

requirements.description: Level 2 (ORGANIZATION_VERIFIED) with an annotations object whose ASCII property names sort differently under RFC 8785 §3.2.3 than under two common alternatives. JCS compares property names as UTF-16 code units, so 10 sorts before 9 (digits compare as characters, not as numbers) and B and Z sort before _ and a (upper case before lower case). The registry signed that order. A conforming verifier ACCEPTs; a verifier that sorts numerically, case-insensitively or by locale collation reconstructs a different signing input and reports a spurious SIGNATURE_INVALID. The non-ASCII half of the rule, code units against code points, is pinned by level-2-attestation-non-bmp-keys.

requirements.name: levels/level-2-multi-defect-subject-and-evidence

specRefs.section: §1 Organization Verification (check order: subject binding before evidence shape)

requirements.description: Check-order fixture with two defects: the validly signed attestation's subject.kid (agent-e5f6a7b8) does not match the declared publicKey.kid (agent-a1b2c3d4), a SUBJECT_MISMATCH, and evidence omits validationTime, a SHAPE_INVALID. The subject binding check precedes the evidence shape check in the contract order, so a conforming verifier MUST reject with SUBJECT_MISMATCH. A verifier that runs every shape check before any binding check reports SHAPE_INVALID and fails this fixture.

requirements.name: levels/level-2-organization-verified
requirements.description: Level 2 (ORGANIZATION_VERIFIED): an AgentCard carrying an organization attestation signed by a trust registry (Ed25519 over the RFC 8785 JCS canonicalization of the attestation object with the signature field excluded). A conforming verifier checks that the attestation subject binds to the declared agentId and kid, verifies the registry signature against the pinned issuer public key, and confirms the pinned validationTime falls inside [verifiedAt, expiresAt]. The issuer key is RFC 8032 §7.1 Test 2 (registry role); the agent key is Test 1.

requirements.name: levels/level-2-subject-mismatch
requirements.description: Negative fixture: an ORGANIZATION_VERIFIED AgentCard carrying a registry attestation that is validly signed and inside its validity window, but whose subject.agentId names a different agent of the same organization (urn:a2a:agent:example.com:payments-bot:v1). subject.kid matches the declared key ID. A conforming verifier MUST reject: the attestation does not bind to the declared agentId. Models replay of an attestation the registry issued to another agent.

requirements.name: levels/level-2-verified-at-not-string
requirements.description: Negative fixture: an ORGANIZATION_VERIFIED attestation whose verifiedAt is an array holding the timestamp string, not the string itself. Every other field is well-formed. A conforming verifier MUST reject at the shape stage: verifiedAt must be a string in YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ form. A verifier that tests the value against a pattern without checking its type can coerce the array to its only element, pass the shape check, and report SIGNATURE_INVALID instead.
